items.title: gstack — Garry Tan's skill pack (design roles)
items.note: Design roles: plan-design-review (7-pass review) and design-shotgun. Best idea: 'Don't make me think' and 'omit, then omit again'.

items.title: Hallmark — design skill that refuses to look AI-made
items.note: 50 themes treated as 'materials'. Gates in tiers: Floor (never ship), Reflex (AI defaults), Finish (craft details).

items.title: DESIGN.md — Google Labs format for design systems
items.note: One file = YAML tokens (colors, type, spacing) + prose explaining why. Portable across projects. Has lint + diff CLI.

items.title: Taste skill — registry of 'AI tells'
items.note: Dated list of things that make a UI look generated (purple gradients, emoji icons, eyebrow labels, same radius everywhere…).

items.title: AI Design Skills — landing page + Figma skills
items.note: Landing-page and Figma-designer skills; SlopScan audits a live page against the same rules.

items.title: Impeccable — design director skill
items.note: Splits PRODUCT.md (who/why) from DESIGN.md (look). Modes: Persuade, Operate, Read, Experience. 'Craft floor' checklist.

items.title: Stageshow — faux product UI for demos
items.note: 'Reads as a real product, simplified to what the viewer needs, framed with intent.' For marketing shots and demos.

items.title: Apple Design (Human Interface Guidelines)
items.note: The reference for clarity, feel, motion and platform conventions.
items.desc: Find documentation and resources for designing great apps for Apple platforms.

items.title: Emil Kowalski — design engineering skills
items.note: Animation decision framework, Apple-style feel, UI cheatsheet (tabular numbers, 65ch lines, scale(0.97) on press).

items.text:
So here it is — @ryolu_ 's talk at @aiDotEngineer  2026 Shanghai.

I shot it handheld on a Xiaomi 15 Ultra, so there's some shake; I fixed as much of it as I could in CapCut. Handheld footage just isn't going to be sharp or steady.

Still, it's the best talk I saw on day 1 of AIE — which is why I'm not posting a text summary. Watch for yourself.

I missed the first minute or so. Ryo opens with the excitement of what AI makes possible, and how seeing what others are building can quickly turn that excitement into anxiety about falling behind.
